candidate_relations.reason: The vitreous biopsy with IDH-1 mutation, ATRX loss, p53 positivity, GFAP/OLIG2 positivity, and Ki-67 ~10% in the context of optic nerve enlargement on MRI supports a high-grade IDH-mutant astrocytic glioma (WHO grade IV glioblastoma per 2021 WHO criteria). 'Glioma, astrocytic' correctly identifies the tumor family but omits the required WHO grade IV designation and the critical anatomical components of optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension that define the full benchmark diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Glioma, astrocytic is the parent category; missing WHO grade IV (glioblastoma) specification, IDH-mutant astrocytoma vs GBM distinction, and the anatomical extension components (optic nerve invasion and intraocular extension)

case_quality_flags: IDH1 mutation with ATRX loss and p53 positivity is more consistent with IDH-mutant astrocytoma grade 4 (WHO 2021) than classic IDH-wildtype GBM; reference diagnosis of 'Glioblastoma WHO grade IV' may reflect older classification or clinical context
Ki-67 ~10% is relatively low for GBM but does not exclude high-grade designation given other molecular markers
